name: pike-north
summary:
The blank walls are fixed: build.nbt now has glazed tall windows on every face of both buildings. The windows were empty holes because the shell parts carve openings to air and the build then locks that air, so later parts couldn't glaze them. Each shell part now glazes its own windows and gives them sash rails, sills, lintels and warm lights.
The Soames-Dunn front now has proper wooden shopfronts and doors under a dark-green awning, and the Starbucks logo sits over its door. Both buildings have storey bands and a cornice course, and Butterworth's 1st Avenue cornice is deeper.
I rebuilt with make.sh, ran check and palette, and looked at all four sides. Footprints, orientation and brick palette are unchanged.

revisions.comment:
Fix round on the composed views. Keep footprints, plots, site orientation and the brick palette. Fix:
1. Both buildings show large blank brick walls. Every street face needs windows: regular rows of tall windows (glass panes in white or dark-green frames, some lit warmly) on every upper storey, with sills and lintels, storey bands and a cornice.
2. The Soames-Dunn street face (on Pike Place, low x) is a row of small shops at ground level: wooden-framed display windows and doors under a long striped or dark-green awning; among them the FIRST STARBUCKS, a brown wooden storefront with a round brown logo sign over the door and the words in cream, and BAVARIAN MEATS beside it; flower boxes under the upper windows.
3. The Butterworth Building's 1st Avenue face (high x): four storeys of red brick with ARCHED windows on the upper floors, shopfronts at street level, a heavy projecting cornice at the top.

The windows were empty holes because the shell parts carve openings to air and the build then locks that air, so later parts couldn't glaze them. Each shell part now glazes its own windows and gives them sash rails, sills, lintels and warm lights.
The Soames-Dunn front now has proper wooden shopfronts and doors under a dark-green awning, and the Starbucks logo sits over its door. Both buildings have storey bands and a cornice course, and Butterworth's 1st Avenue cornice is deeper.
I rebuilt with make.sh, ran check and palette, and looked at all four sides. Footprints, orientation and brick palette are unchanged.
applied: 1 – windows on every face: Soames (Pike Place front, the face above the lower roof, north and south ends, alley sides, court side) and Butterworth (Pike Place back, north and south ends) now have regular rows of tall 2–3-wide windows on every upper storey. Each has glass set one block in, a cut_sandstone lintel and a smooth_sandstone sill. A frame bar runs across each window: dark green (green_concrete) on Soames-Dunn, white (white_concrete) on Butterworth. About 2 in 3 have a warm shroomlight just behind the glass.

1 – storey bands and cornice: pale bands at each storey on the Soames rear ranges (y17, y24) and on Butterworth's back and ends (y17, y24, y30). The dark roof-deck edge that showed on the walls is now a pale course at the top of the wall. The Butterworth back gets a cut_sandstone frieze (in place of the red_nether_bricks band) under a smooth_sandstone top course.

2 – Soames shopfronts: every bay has a wooden-framed display window over a bulkhead, a pair of doors under a brown glass transom, a corner post and a head beam. The awning is now dark green (green_concrete) with the dark oak brackets and lanterns kept.

2 – Starbucks: spruce storefront and spruce doors in bays 4–5. The round brown logo moved to sit over the door (bay 5), and STARBUCKS is in cream-white letters on brown. Bavarian Meats is kept beside it, and flower boxes stay under the upper windows.

3 – Butterworth 1st Avenue front: four storeys of brick, arched F3/F4 windows and shopfronts at street level as before. I added a stone belt course at y17 and made the cornice heavier: a row of stone blocks under it, a second course on top and a slab cap.

Inspection: check shows no floating or orphan blocks from this round. 19 floating lights, some loose blocks and 1 unsupported banner remain from the earlier finish part, all present in v1. The palette check flags green_concrete and shroomlight as outliers; they are kept because they are the green frames, green awning and lit windows you asked for.
skipped: Cornice on Butterworth's Pike Place back and on the ends can't project: it would sit outside the footprint, and the wall is already on the edge cells. The nearest sensible thing is a flush pale frieze and top course at the roof line.
I went with dark green for the Soames awning rather than stripes (you offered either).
Interiors behind the glass are not dressed beyond the warm glow blocks (exterior-only build).
